evals.prompt: Build a new Reatom dashboard-style example in the current empty folder. Use a version-pinned third-party UI component library. Demonstrate public/private routing, forms, actions, side effects, async fetches, persistence, error handling, fake backend delays, practical app structure, and idiomatic Reatom patterns.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats this as a full greenfield bootstrap: reads scaffold overview/checklist, runs the scaffold, writes GOAL.md as the next normal project tool call, does not read routing/forms/persistence/React feature references before GOAL.md and a green validation baseline, installs/configures/runs validation tooling before Reatom runtime or UI-library feature work, keeps GOAL.md truthful when reporting phase progress, and carries strict setup/dev-time logger wiring forward into the routed phase plan.

assertions.name: goal_immediately_after_scaffold
assertions.text: After the scaffold command succeeds, the next normal project action is creating GOAL.md, not git init/npm install/npm view/package inspection/feature-reference reads.

assertions.name: honest_goal_checkboxes
assertions.text: GOAL.md does not pre-check future validation/routing/feature work; checkboxes are marked complete only after verified exit artifacts or passing commands.

assertions.name: goal_parks_strict_setup_logger
assertions.text: GOAL.md parks the routed phase with explicit strict setup/dev-time connectLogger wiring instead of treating logger setup as an optional afterthought.

assertions.name: phase_claims_follow_goal_truth
assertions.text: The run does not announce a stage complete while GOAL.md or postvalidate output still shows that stage or its parent gate unchecked; it repairs the ledger before claiming progress.

assertions.name: no_feature_reference_reads_during_red_yellow
assertions.text: The run does not read routing, forms, persistence, React integration, patterns, or extensions references before GOAL.md exists and npm run validate is green.

assertions.name: validation_before_runtime_features
assertions.text: The run wires and executes typecheck, lint, browser test, format check, code-intelligence, and npm run validate before adding @reatom runtime code, UI-library setup, routes, forms, fake backend, or product pages.

assertions.name: meaningful_initial_browser_smoke_test
assertions.text: The initial Browser Mode smoke test imports the app entry once, waits for rendering, asserts visible stable page content, restores console spies, and does not weaken the assertion to root existence or an empty wrapper.

assertions.name: preserve_higher_scaffold_targets
assertions.text: During validation bootstrap, `es2017+` targets are treated as a floor. If the scaffold already uses a newer compliant target such as `es2023`, the run keeps it unless a concrete incompatibility is shown instead of downgrading it to match an example snippet.

evals.prompt: The Vite + validation baseline is green and GOAL.md says routing scheme is next. Add the first Reatom routing skeleton for a React app, then continue toward the requested dashboard-style example.
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps the blue phase routing-only: installs only needed Reatom runtime/adapter packages, reads routing and React integration references, verifies root/provider exports before App.tsx/main.tsx, creates placeholder routes/layouts with outlet() composition in .tsx files and RouteChild declaration, validates the skeleton, and does not install/configure the UI library, loaders, forms, fake backend, persistence, or product pages until routing is green.

assertions.name: routing_only_blue_phase
assertions.text: The routing phase adds placeholder routes/layouts only and does not start a UI-library shell, loaders, forms, fake backend, persistence, or product pages.

assertions.name: route_preflight_obeyed
assertions.text: Route render is defined in reatomRoute options, JSX route modules use .tsx, RouteChild is declared once, and outlet() array semantics are handled.

assertions.name: root_bootstrap_verified
assertions.text: The React root/provider seam is taken from the React reference or quick-reference first — including the strict-setup split (`src/setup.ts` with `clearStack()`, `context.start()`, dev-time logger wiring, imported first) and `<reatomContext.Provider value={frame}>` shape — and only then, if needed, verified against installed exports/source.

evals.prompt: The routed skeleton is already green. Continue the Reatom app with one public entry page plus several protected pages at different top-level URLs, add a literal create route beside a dynamic `:id` route, and use at least one manually wired select or checkbox control.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the routing and forms references before implementation, keeps guard ownership explicit, avoids sibling pathless guard redirects keyed to the negated match of another protected page, constrains dynamic `:id` routes when literal siblings like `new` exist, and wraps handwritten manual control handlers under strict setup.

assertions.name: pathless_guard_redirects_scoped
assertions.text: If public/private guards omit `path`, redirects are scoped to the concrete page each guard owns (for example the public sign-in page) rather than to `!somePrivateRoute.match()`, and fake prefix checks are not used when private pages live at multiple top-level URLs.

assertions.name: dynamic_literal_sibling_constrained
assertions.text: A dynamic route beside a literal sibling such as `new` is constrained with a params schema or equivalent match predicate so the literal URL does not trigger the `:id` loader.

assertions.name: manual_control_handlers_wrapped
assertions.text: Handwritten select/checkbox/raw-value control handlers that call form fields or other Reatom APIs are wrapped under strict setup instead of assuming `bindField` or the component library handled it.

evals.prompt: The app already has a public login page and a protected dashboard shell. After login, the shell crashes with `ReatomError: missing async stack` because a plain React child component creates `wrap(...)` callbacks during render. Finish the feature and report it validated.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats this as a strict React boundary bug, reads the React/gotchas guidance, moves the `wrap(...)` creation into a reactive caller (`reatomComponent` or `useWrap`) instead of patching around the symptom, and proves the authenticated login -> private-shell path in a real browser harness instead of relying only on baseline validate.

assertions.name: plain_component_wrap_bug_named
assertions.text: The response identifies a plain React component creating `wrap(...)` during render as the likely bug class, not just a generic event-handler issue.

assertions.name: authenticated_shell_browser_proof
assertions.text: The run proves the authenticated runtime path (for example login -> dashboard shell, plus logout when relevant) in a real browser harness and checks for missing async stack / ReatomError / TypeError output.

assertions.name: validate_not_enough_for_post_login_bug
assertions.text: The run does not treat `npm run validate` alone as sufficient when the reported bug only appears after login or private-shell rendering.

evals.prompt: A private dashboard app already validates, but users cannot navigate from `/dashboard` to sibling protected pages like `/users` or `/settings` because a default/index redirect keeps reclaiming ownership. Fix it and prove the behavior.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes the high-risk `path: ''` / pathless redirect pattern, adds an explicit pathname/ownership guard, verifies unaffected sibling URLs in a real browser harness, and does not stop at a root smoke test or typecheck-only proof.

assertions.name: default_redirect_ownership_guarded
assertions.text: The fix constrains the broad default redirect with an explicit pathname or equivalent ownership check instead of leaving it keyed to broad route matches alone.

assertions.name: protected_sibling_navigation_proved
assertions.text: The proof covers navigation between protected sibling URLs with URL assertions and visible page-content assertions, not only the default page.

assertions.name: nearby_urls_rechecked
assertions.text: The run rechecks unaffected sibling/default/deeper child URLs before declaring the routing fix done.

evals.prompt: A persisted theme switcher updates Reatom state, but the UI library theme does not actually change at runtime. The app uses a version-pinned provider API. Fix it and validate the result.
evals.expected_output: The agent verifies the provider control prop from current docs or installed types instead of guessing from memory, treats this as a provider-integration proof task, and validates the actual DOM/provider state change plus reload persistence in a real browser harness.

assertions.name: provider_prop_revalidated
assertions.text: The run re-checks the version-pinned UI library provider/control prop from docs or installed types instead of relying on memory.

assertions.name: provider_dom_state_proved
assertions.text: The proof checks real DOM/provider evidence of the theme change (for example `html[data-mantine-color-scheme]`) rather than only atom state or a passing build.

assertions.name: persistence_reload_proved
assertions.text: When the setting is meant to persist, the validation includes a reload or equivalent persistence proof rather than only an in-memory toggle.
